reason: The intro of the compute optimized page states the design goal (compute intensive applications that benefit from high performance processors) and lists every example the claim names.
The quote states the balance of compute, memory and networking, equal proportions, and the web server and code repository examples.
The quote is the same sentence as the claim: fast performance for workloads that process large data sets in memory.
The quote states high, sequential read and write access to very large data sets on local storage and tens of thousands of low-latency random IOPS.
Under the Availability Zones question the quote states distinct independent infrastructure, generators and cooling not shared, and that fires, tornados or flooding would only affect a single AZ.

The quote states AWS recommends evaluating Bare Metal for workloads that need hardware virtualization extensions and are performance sensitive or have strict latency requirements; all conditions are kept.
The quote states per-second calculation, cumulative usage per instance per month shown in decimal hours, and the 1 hour 10 minutes 4 seconds = 1.1677 example.
The quote states usage is billed while in the running state, that you must stop or terminate to avoid further usage charges, and billing starts on the transition to running.
Under the question on when to choose a burstable instance, the quote advises dedicated CPU instances such as M or C when CPU use is consistently much higher than the baseline.
The quote states that without a need for the capacity reservation you should buy a regional RI, which gives AZ and instance size flexibility.
The quote states that to take advantage of the capacity reservation you should buy an RI in a specific AZ.
The quote states a Capacity Block can be purchased as far out as eight weeks into the future or as soon as now when capacity is available; maximum is correctly marked.

The quote and its context state Capacity Blocks give access to the highest-performing GPU instances for ML, ensure GPU capacity, and are delivered in EC2 UltraClusters for the best network latency and throughput.
The quote states a Capacity Block cannot be modified or canceled once it is reserved.
The quote states AWS begins terminating running instances around 30 minutes before the Capacity Block expires.
The quote states the key difference exactly: scheduled future-dated GPU capacity for ML versus flexible immediate capacity assurance for any workload without advance scheduling or a fixed end date.
The quote states the reservable number is based on the On-Demand instance limit minus instances already running; the context supports the per-Region scope and that the limit can be raised.
The quote states ending by cancel or end time after the commitment period of future-dated reservations, and that running instances are unaffected by changes, deletion or expiration.
Under the question on modifying a started reservation, the quote names the number of instances, the match criteria and the end date.
The quote states active Capacity Reservations can be shared with other accounts or within an AWS Organization through AWS RAM.
The quote states Capacity Reservations are for strict capacity requirements of current or future business-critical workloads needing long or short-term capacity assurance.
The quote states the tie to AZ, instance type, platform and tenancy, and that Open match criteria cover matching running or new instances when there is enough excess capacity.
The quote states that to receive a history of all EC2 API calls, including VPC and EBS, you turn on CloudTrail.
The quote states a stopped instance starts in the cluster placement group it was in and the start fails if capacity is not available in that group.
The quote states Convertible RIs let you change the instance type, operating system, tenancy or payment option during the term.
The quote states there are no exchange limits for Convertible RIs.
The quote states there is no exchange fee but a one-time true-up charge for pricing differences may apply.
The quote names the three-year commitment for a significant discount, uncertainty about future instance needs, and benefiting from price changes; the claim keeps all three.
Under the question on instances in different AZs, the quote states each instance is charged for its data in and data out at corresponding Data Transfer rates; the claim adds nothing beyond it.
The quote states Inter-Region Data Transfer Out for the first instance and Inter-Region Data Transfer In for the second.
The quote states RIs that received an AWS discount, such as RI Volume Discount, are not eligible for sale on the EC2 RI Marketplace.
The quote states you do not need an Elastic IP address for all your instances.
The quote states EC2 Fleet has no additional charge and you pay only for the resources it launches.
The answer 'No' to the failover question plus the quote state EC2 Fleet keeps trying to meet the requested Spot capacity.
The quote states an On-Demand instance launched by EC2 Fleet that matches an existing RI receives the RI discount; the matching condition is kept.
The quote states multi-region EC2 Fleet requests are not supported.
The quote states a 40% baseline and scaling up to 100% CPU for 95% of the time over a 24-hour window.
The quote states G-series for graphics, gaming, spatial computing, AI/ML inference and single-node training, and P-series for AI inference and training of large foundation models.
In context 'both the cases' means hibernate and stop; the quote states the private IP and the Elastic IP (if applicable) remain the same.
The quote states RAM data is always encrypted when moved to the EBS root volume and root volume encryption is enforced at instance launch.
